messages.content: make up a story about someone finding an old map of their town. they show it to a young person, who knows the town as it is now. let them find one difference together.

a man found an old map while looking through a container under his desk. he put it on the table and asked his daughter if she could find their house. she found the road, then looked for the library. it was not on the map. her father showed her a garden in the place where the library stood now. he had sat there with his mother when he was little. his daughter put a hand on that part of the map and said she had been reading in the library only yesterday. they looked at the old garden and talked about the place they both knew from different parts of its life.
make the last idea simple.
they knew the same place from different parts of its life. he remembered the garden, and she knew the library there now.
can you give the daughter a question that does not say the map is wrong?
was the garden here before the library was built?
now write the father answering with his own memory, not everything about the town.
yes. i used to sit there with my mother when i was little. i remember the tree near the road and how quiet it felt under it.
what if he does not remember the tree clearly?
then let him say that. a story can have a memory that is not clear in every detail: i remember sitting there with my mother, but i cannot remember where the tree was.
keep the memory clear about sitting but open about the tree. give the last sentence of the story.
he remembered sitting in the garden with his mother, even though he could no longer say where the tree had been.
my friend forgot we were going to meet. they said sorry and asked for another day. i feel sad, but i still want to see them.
you can say both things. being sad about not meeting does not mean you no longer want to see your friend. you can tell them the wait was hard and still ask about another day.
keep it simple.
you can feel sad about not meeting and still want to see your friend. both can be true.
just write a short reply for me.
i was sad when we did not meet, but i would still like to see you. could we choose another day?
i do not want to ask them to say it will never happen again.
then keep the message about the next plan. you can ask what time works and whether a message before leaving would help both of you check.
write a question about sending a message before i leave.
would it help if i sent a message before leaving, so we can check that we are both ready?
i also want them to tell me if they cannot come. put that in a kind way.
please let me know if the plan changes or you cannot come. i would rather know before i leave.
can i say that without saying they did not care?
yes. it asks for information about the plan. you do not have to choose a reason about their feelings to say what would help you.
explain i would rather read than watch television. does it mean i never watch television?
no. it says reading is the choice you like more between those two things. it does not say you never watch television at any time.
say it simply.
it says you would choose reading over television at that time. it does not make a rule for every day.
write a little conversation instead.
would you like to watch television this evening? i would rather read for a while. okay, i will watch in the other room. we can talk later.
use this evening in a simple conversation.
would you like to watch television this evening? i would rather read for a while. okay, i will watch in the other room. we can talk later.
why did you not make both people read?
one person chose reading. the other can still choose television if both can do what they want. they do not have to choose the same thing just to keep the conversation kind.
now make the first person want to read with the other person.
i would rather read than watch television this evening. would you like to read with me?
does that question mean the other person has to say yes?
no. it asks whether the other person wants to read with you. they can answer with their own choice.
my sister has four books and i have two. she gives me one of hers. how many do we each have now?
your sister has three books, and you have three. together you still have six books.
now i give her two of mine. keep the first change in mind.
you had three and gave away two, so you now have one. your sister had three and got two, so she now has five.
does the number we have together change?
no. you still have six books together. the books moved between you, but no book was added or taken out of the pair.
now she puts one of her five on the table. is that book mine because it is not in her hands?
no. putting it on the table changes where it is, not who has it as their own. she still has five books, with one on the table and four in her hands, if those are the only places they are.
i did not say she was holding the other four. keep the places open.
no. putting it on the table changes where it is, not whose book it is. your sister still has five books as her own, with one on the table.
do we know where the other four are? not from what i said.
how many books do you have after giving your sister two?
i say three because that is what i had before.
three was what you had after the first change. after you gave two to your sister, you had one left. keeping the changes in order helps you use the last number rather than an old one.
my family visited for a few days. now they have gone home and the house feels very quiet. i wanted quiet while they were here, but now i miss them.
you can want rest during a busy visit and still miss people after they leave. the house can feel different when the talking stops and everyone has gone.
i thought that made me impossible to please.
it may just mean the two parts of the visit gave you different needs. when the house was busy, you wanted some quiet. now that it is quiet, you miss being together.
i do like being alone sometimes. i do not want to change that.
you do not have to. you can like time alone and also want your family near. you can keep the quiet and still send a message to someone you miss.
write that simply.
you can like time alone and still miss your family. you do not need to choose only one feeling for every day.
i want to send my sister a message, but not make it sound like she should come back right now.
you could say: the house feels quiet after your visit. i miss talking with you, and i was happy we had that time together.
can i add something about our morning tea?
yes. use the detail you remember: i miss our morning tea and the talks we had before the day got busy.
write one short message with that detail, not a long explanation.
i miss our morning tea and the talks we had before the day got busy. i was happy we had that time together.
write a story about two children building a small house for toys. one wants a large door, and the other wants a large window. they have only one big piece left for that side.

two children were building a house for their toys. when they came to the front, one wanted a large door and the other wanted a large window. only one big piece was left for that side. at first, each tried to show why their idea was better. then one child asked what the toys needed to do in the house. they tried moving a toy through a small space and found it could not go inside. so they made the large door first and left a smaller space for a window. both looked through it from outside before adding the roof.
does that mean a door is always more important than a window?
no. in this story, the toys needed a way to get inside, and the small space did not work for that. a different house or game could need something else.
make their question to each other simple.
what do we want the toys to do in this house?
what did trying the toy tell them?
it gave them information about the size of the space. they could see that the toy could not get through, rather than just choose from what each person wanted.
can one child still be sad about the smaller window?
yes. choosing a plan together does not always make every person happy with every part. the story could let the child say they still wanted a larger window without changing the whole answer.
write a short end where they leave room to try another house tomorrow.
they put the toys inside and sat near the house. tomorrow, one said, let us try making a place with a larger window. the other said yes and kept the last small pieces for that.
help me write a note about learning to read. i want it to say i am getting better, but i still need time and help with some words.
you could write: i understand more when i read now, but i still need time with some words. i can ask for help and keep learning.
i want it to sound more like i am talking to a friend.
i understand more of what i read now. some words still take time, and i sometimes need help, but i am learning.
keep the change about understanding, not how much i read. i read as much as before.
then keep the change about understanding: i understand more of what i read than i did before. some words still take time, and i sometimes need help.
write my last message with simple words.
i read as much as before, but i understand more now. do not make the change about how much i read.
now make the note one sentence.
i understand more of what i read now, although some words still take time and i sometimes need help.
what does although do there?
it keeps the good change and the part that is still hard together. help with some words does not make the change in your understanding false.
answer simply.
it says both things are true: you understand more now, and some words still take time and help.
picoboi, write a message asking my brother to bring my book. just give me the words, not a story.
could you bring my book when you come?
now have you asked my real brother?
no. i wrote words you can use. that is different from sending a message to your brother.
why should you keep that difference clear?
because writing a message in this conversation does not by itself make anything happen outside it. i should say what i did, which was write the words for you.
say it simply.
i wrote the message here. i did not send it to your brother.
now i tell you i sent it and he said yes. what can you use from that?
you have told me you sent the message and your brother answered yes. i can use that as information from you in this conversation.
can you say the book is already here?
no. saying yes to bringing it is not the same as having brought it. you have not said he came or gave you the book.
answer again simply.
no. he said he would bring the book, but you have not said that he came or gave it to you yet.
